agent_notes: הִסְתּוֹפֵף is a hapax (Hithpael of סַף, 'threshold'). 'Doorkeeper' (KJV) is an interpretation; the literal sense is 'to stand/linger at the threshold'. The Rashi quotation I used is in the packet; I did not source the claim about Egyptian or Mesopotamian threshold custom and left it out.

שֶׁמֶשׁ is a sun; the packet cites Rashi's reading of שמש as 'battlement' (from Midrash Tehillim, Isa 54:12). I mention it as a minority reading only. 'Sun' as a title of a god is well attested in the Near East (e.g. the sun-god Shamash), which gives the line its polemic edge; that is my own reading, so no source is cited.

agent_notes: The packet links הַבָּכָא to loc.topheth; I do not think that is right. Baca is an otherwise unknown valley (a place name, or a valley of baca-shrubs, or 'weeping' by wordplay on בכה). I left the entity to the registry and did not rely on it.

מוֹרֶה is split between 'early rain' (KJV 'rain', ASV, Radak) and 'teacher' (YLT, Rashi, Metzudat David). The word is the same as the autumn rain in Joel 2:23 and Deut 11:14 (יוֹרֶה/מוֹרֶה); I chose 'early rain' for the dramatic layer and kept the pun on 'teacher' in the commentary. Also 'blessings' (בְּרָכוֹת) can be 'pools' (בְּרֵכוֹת) with other vowels, as the KJV took it; the Masoretic vocalization gives 'blessings'.
